hero.title: Can you swap to a cheaper car?
hero.p1: Compare keeping your financed vehicle with replacement options. The decision number is cash all-in monthly — loan payment plus insurance, maintenance, and fuel or electricity. Economic / TCO with exit equity is shown as context so depreciation does not hide in the payment alone.
hero.p2: province-aware vehicle taxes (including BC PST-116 trade-in rules), EV rebates, multi-scenario trade-in ranges, per-scenario cash targets, informational terminal-equity TCO, field overrides, and a reverse max-budget solve for your cash all-in goal.

methodology.title: How the math works
methodology.p1: Everything runs in your browser; inputs never leave your device. Cash all-in monthly (loan + insurance + M&O + fuel) is the decision metric — each scenario sets its own cash target for under/over and max-budget solve. Economic monthly is informational: net horizon ownership cost including exit equity, so you can see depreciation context without forcing a hard-to-intuit TCO budget.
methodology.p2: Auto loans use monthly compounding (APR ÷ periods per year), not Canadian mortgage semi-annual compounding. Vehicle taxes follow provincial rules; BC applies PST-116 (rate from full price, tax on net after trade-in). Rules last reviewed for {{rulesDate}}.
methodology.economicBody: Following AAA and Edmunds, depreciation is modeled as purchase value minus estimated resale at your ownership horizon — not as a separate monthly charge stacked on loan principal. Auto retained value uses an age-aware curve; override retained % manually if you prefer. Exit equity = exit value minus remaining loan balance. Economic monthly is shown for comparison only; your cash target and max-budget solve ignore it.
methodology.taxBody: For dealer purchases in BC, the PST rate is looked up from the full purchase price, then applied to purchase price minus trade-in. GST is 5% on the same net. Federal luxury tax (if any) uses the pre-tax price and is not reduced by trade-in. Private sales do not get a trade-in tax credit.
methodology.maxBody: Operating costs are subtracted from this scenario's cash target to get loan payment room. That payment is inverted to a max amount financed, then a binary search finds the highest pre-tax purchase price whose taxes, rebates, trade equity, and down payment produce that financed amount.
methodology.disclaimer: Not financial or tax advice. Estimates for educational sensitivity analysis. Retained value is your assumption, not a Black Book or Edmunds forecast. Confirm with your dealer, lender, and provincial registry.
